Advancing autonomous science through smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR) today announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft to support the development of smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem that connects technologies across Danaher while remaining open to the broader laboratory ecosystem, helping scientists move from scientific questions to experimental evidence faster. The partnership seeks to combine Danaher's scientific, workflow and instrumentation expertise with Microsoft's AI technologies, making experimental execution more streamlined and insights more readily available to translate discovery into human impact.

The partnership is focused on accelerating the development of a common agentic platform for instrument control and insight generation. The platform is built on Microsoft technology: Microsoft Azure for secure, compliant cloud infrastructure, and Microsoft Foundry to power the AI agents that interpret results and guide instrument control. Its goal is to enable reuse and interoperability across technologies, so specialized products can be built on a shared foundation, while remaining open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories.

While the companies are continuing to develop this platform, the first commercial applications will reach Danaher customers this year, including MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant, Molecular Devices' software for its high-content cellular imaging systems, designed to provide product support. Additional next-generation, agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses that use this platform are planned for 2027.

"Danaher's businesses bring deep scientific and instrument expertise to customers every day," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, President and CEO of Danaher. "With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher. Through context and learning, that foundation can continuously inform the next experiment and the best analysis. This partnership is an important step toward making laboratories not just connected, but intelligent."

As part of this partnership, smart, agent-enabled instruments are being designed with the goal of supporting scientists across four critical activities:

  • Translating scientific intent into experimental plans, instrument setup and methods
  • Controlling instrument hardware within defined safety boundaries and with user oversight, while guiding execution and troubleshooting
  • Interpreting results and identifying quality issues in real time
  • Recommending corrective actions and next experiments for scientist review

AI-assisted instruments are intended to simplify complex scientific workflows. In preliminary internal testing, novice scientists conducting an AI-assisted experiment on a Leica microscope took up to 83% less time and up to 68% fewer steps to complete than a novice working without the AI assistant, while producing high-quality data and completing the experiment in a time comparable to an expert.

"Danaher's scientific expertise, combined with Microsoft's AI platform, aims to give scientists more choice and control, and more time for discovery," said Deb Cupp, Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer, Microsoft Global Enterprise. "This partnership aligns with our goal to help translate AI into real-world impact."

The partnership is designed to advance Danaher's broader strategy for AI and autonomous science by connecting intelligence at the instrument with data, laboratory workflows and the physical execution of experiments. Intelligent instruments are a first step. As instruments and laboratory systems become more connected and interoperable, Danaher believes experimental results can help scientists determine what to do next, supporting discovery through increasingly connected and autonomous workflows under scientific oversight.

Company Highlights Proactive Customer Protection Measures, Continued Store Operations and Established Risk Mitigation Policies

NASHVILLE, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Neighborhood Intelligence, Inc. (Nasdaq: NXH) today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, The Container Store, has restored its website and systems following a cybersecurity incident this past weekend.

Upon detecting suspicious activity, the company immediately activated its established cybersecurity protocols and proactively suspended online order-taking at The Container Store to protect its customer information and its systems. All retail locations remained open, serving customers through alternative transaction-processing procedures.

Marcus Lemonis, Chief Executive Officer of Neighborhood Intelligence, commented:

“I am extremely proud of how our technology and operational teams responded. We made the deliberate decision to prioritize the protection of our customers and our systems while keeping our stores open and serving customers. Our established protocols, combined with the expertise of our outside partners, allowed us to respond with discipline and restore operations in a controlled manner. I want to thank our associates and partners for their exceptional work and our customers for their patience and continued support.”

As part of its established response protocols, the company engaged leading independent cybersecurity experts to assist with the investigation, containment and restoration efforts. Our investigation into this event is ongoing, however we do not believe that this incident impacted the security of any customer financial data because The Container Store does not store or maintain consumer financial or payment information.

The company also maintains established risk mitigation procedures and business interruption insurance coverage designed to help manage operational and financial exposure associated with incidents of this nature.

The incident was isolated to The Container Store. We expect a minimal impact on consolidated revenue for the quarter, with any impact on profitability expected to be mitigated by our business interruption insurance. The company’s other businesses, including Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY and Kirkland’s, remained unaffected. The company continues to expect sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter.

About Neighborhood Intelligence, Inc.

Neighborhood Intelligence (Nasdaq: NXH), previously Bed Bath & Beyond, Inc., is a data and technology company organized around three interconnected pillars: Omni-Channel Retail, Home Services and Home Ownership. Its portfolio includes Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY, Kirkland’s, The Container Store, Elfa and Closet Works, along with its expanding Home Services and Home Ownership businesses. The Company also includes a blockchain asset portfolio inclusive of tZERO, GrainChain, and other assets. For more information, please visit neighborhoodintelligence.com.

Former SaskPower, Petroleum Technology Research Centre and MAX Power leader joins NUE's Board following the Company's annual general meeting

Vancouver, British Columbia and Regina, Saskatchewan--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - NUE Power Corp. (CSE: NUE) (OTC Pink: NUEPF) (FSE: NUE1) ("NUE" or the "Company") announces that, following its annual general meeting of shareholders held on November 19, 2026 (the "Meeting"), Ranjith ("Ran") Narayanasamy, P.Eng., has been appointed by the Company's Board of Directors (the "Board") and subsequently named Chairman of the Board at a meeting of the Board held after the Meeting.

As announced on October 28, 2026, Mr. Narayanasamy helped establish NUE's presence in Regina, Saskatchewan, including its acceptance as a tenant at Innovation Saskatchewan's Collider.

Message from the CEO

"Appointing Ran as Chairman is a deliberate step as NUE seeks to move from originating projects to monetizing them," said Broderick Gunning, Chief Executive Officer of NUE. "Our develop-to-divest model depends on three things: advancing projects to the point where they create value, completing commercial transactions on the right terms, and accessing capital with discipline.

"Ran has led at a provincial utility, a research centre and a public company that attracted investment during his tenure, and he has already helped us build our base in Saskatchewan. That mix of technical, regional and capital markets experience is what we want leading our Board as we work toward potential offtake agreements and project sales."

About Ranjith Narayanasamy

Mr. Narayanasamy has more than two decades of experience in the energy sector. He served as Chief Executive Officer of MAX Power Mining Corp. (CSE: MAXX) from December 1, 2025 to October 13, 2026.

Before MAX Power, he was President and Chief Executive Officer of the Petroleum Technology Research Centre in Regina, where he led research programs involving carbon capture, utilization and storage, geothermal energy, hydrogen and compressed-air energy storage.

Previously, he spent 17 years at SaskPower, with senior roles across transmission and distribution, project management, hydroelectric development and supply chain. He holds a Master of Engineering and an MBA from the University of Regina and is a registered Professional Engineer in Saskatchewan. His recognitions include the Premier's Award for Excellence in the Public Service and the Queen Elizabeth II Platinum Jubilee Medal, and he was recently named one of the University of Regina Faculty of Engineering and Applied Science's Accomplished Alumni of the past 50 years. In 2026, he was also named a finalist for the Emerging Hydrogen Leader Award at the Canadian Hydrogen Convention.

"I am honoured to take on the role of Chairman," said Mr. Narayanasamy. "My focus will be on strong governance, disciplined capital deployment, strategic relationships and meaningful Indigenous partnership as NUE seeks to move into its next phase."

Results of Annual General Meeting

At the Meeting, shareholders fixed the number of directors at five, elected each of Broderick Gunning, Eugene Hodgson, Bold Batsukh, Peter Espig and Tony Clement as directors and appointed TZR LLP, Chartered Professional Accountants, as auditor of the Company for the ensuing year, authorizing the directors to fix its remuneration. All matters put before the Meeting were approved. Following the Meeting, the Board consists of Ranjith Narayanasamy (Chairman), Broderick Gunning, Eugene Hodgson, Peter Espig and Tony Clement.

Resignation of Director

Following the Meeting, Bold Batsukh resigned as a director of the Company. The Board thanks Mr. Batsukh for his service and contribution to the Company.

(CSE: NUE) (OTC Pink: NUEPF) (FSE: NUE1) is an energy infrastructure development company focused on the origination, development and advancement of integrated power and energy-park opportunities. Operating a develop-to-divest model, the Company emphasizes strategic site positioning, grid access and stage-gated development across markets serving compute-intensive and large-load industrial demand.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Roxmore Resources Inc. At the Meeting, Securityholders will be asked to approve the previously-announced plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) (the "Arrangement") pursuant to which a wholly-owned subsidiary of SSR Mining Inc. ("SSR") will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Roxmore (the "Roxmore Shares") for consideration per Roxmore Share of $6.75 in cash and 0.33 of a common share of RoxCore Resources Inc. ("SpinCo"), a new exploration company that will hold Roxmore's Rattlesnake Hills Project, Newton Project and Shabu River Property and will be capitalized with US$10 million in cash, all as more particularly described in the Circular.

Unanimous Recommendation of the Board

The board of directors of Roxmore (the "Board"), after receiving legal and financial advice, has unanimously determined that the Arrangement is fair and reasonable to Securityholders and in the best interests of Roxmore, and unanimously recommends that Securityholders vote FOR the Arrangement at the Meeting. The factors considered by the Board are detailed in the Circular and include:

  • Significant Premium: The consideration implies total consideration of approximately $7.25 per Roxmore Share (including the estimated value of the SpinCo share consideration of $0.50 per Roxmore Share), representing a premium of approximately 58% to the 20-day volume-weighted average trading price ("VWAP") of the Roxmore Shares and approximately 36% to the closing price of the Roxmore Shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange, in each case as of October 9, 2026, the last trading day prior to the announcement of the Arrangement. The cash consideration alone represents a premium of approximately 47% to the 20-day VWAP.
  • Certainty of Value and Immediate Liquidity: The $6.75 per Roxmore Share in cash provides certainty of value and immediate liquidity without exposure to future dilution or to commodity price, construction, development or execution risk.
  • Continued Exposure to Exploration Upside: Former holders of Roxmore securities are expected to own approximately 85.01% of SpinCo, which will be led by John Dorward and other members of Roxmore's existing technical and executive team and is expected to have US$10 million in cash and no debt. SSR will retain a 14.99% strategic equity interest in SpinCo, which the Board views as an endorsement of SpinCo's exploration upside potential.
  • Fairness Opinions: Each of ATB Cormark, Canaccord Genuity and SCP Resource Finance has provided an opinion to the Board to the effect that, as of October 12, 2026, and based upon and subject to the assumptions, limitations and qualifications set out therein, the consideration to be received by the holders of Roxmore Shares pursuant to the Arrangement is fair, from a financial point of view, to such holders.
  • Strong Support: The directors and officers of Roxmore and L1 Capital Pty Ltd, Roxmore's largest shareholder, who together beneficially own, or exercise control or direction over, approximately 23.15% of the outstanding Roxmore Shares as of the record date for the Meeting, have entered into voting agreements to vote in favour of the Arrangement.

Additional information regarding the reasons for the Board's recommendation and the risks related to the Arrangement is contained in the Circular.

Interim Order

The Company is also pleased to announce that, on November 16, 2026, it obtained an interim order (the "Interim Order") from the Supreme Court of British Columbia (the "Court") providing for the calling and holding of the Meeting and certain other procedural matters in connection with the Arrangement. The Meeting is to be held in accordance with the terms of the Interim Order.

The Meeting

The Meeting will be held in a hybrid format at 8:30 a.m. (Toronto time) on December 16, 2026, in person at 155 Wellington Street West, 40th floor, Toronto, Ontario, and virtually via live webcast at https://meetings.lumiconnect.com/400-181-979-094 (password "roxmore2026"), subject to any adjournment or postponement thereof. Securityholders of record as of the close of business on November 5, 2026 are entitled to receive notice of and to vote at the Meeting.

At the Meeting, Securityholders will be asked to consider and, if deemed advisable, pass a special resolution approving the Arrangement (the "Arrangement Resolution"). In order to become effective, the Arrangement Resolution must be approved by (i) not less than two-thirds of the votes cast by holders of Roxmore Shares, (ii) not less than two-thirds of the votes cast by Securityholders, voting together as a single class, and (iii) a simple majority of the votes cast by holders of Roxmore Shares, excluding the votes of certain related parties of Roxmore, as required under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions, in each case present (virtually or in person) or represented by proxy at the Meeting. If the Arrangement Resolution is approved, holders of Roxmore Shares will also be asked to consider and, if deemed advisable, approve an omnibus equity incentive plan for SpinCo.

The hearing for the final order of the Court is expected to take place on December 18, 2026 and, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of closing conditions, the Arrangement is expected to close in December 2026 or January 2027.

  • Adds One of the Nation's Leading Mechanical Platforms with More Than 119 Years of Operating History and Approximately 1,600 Employees, Including 1,200 Union Craft Workforce
  • Enhances Technical Capabilities Through Industry-Leading Engineering, Prefabrication, Preconstruction and Self-Perform Execution Expertise
  • Expands MasTec's Participation in Fast-Growing Mission-Critical Infrastructure Markets Including Aviation and Defense, Pharmaceutical, Healthcare, Technology and Advanced Manufacturing
  • Creates Significant Opportunities to Expand Recurring Service and Maintenance Revenue Supporting Operational Data Centers and Other Diversified Markets
  • Expected to Be Immediately Accretive to Revenue, Earnings Per Share, Adjusted EBITDA and Cash Flow from Operations

CORAL GABLES, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

MasTec, Inc. (NYSE: MTZ) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Murphy Corporation ("Murphy"), one of the largest and most respected mechanical contractors (“the Transaction”) in the United States. Founded in 1907 and continuously family owned and operated for more than 119 years, Murphy has built a scaled, full-service platform providing mechanical, plumbing and process infrastructure solutions across mission-critical end markets. With approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals and national execution capabilities, Murphy serves a diversified portfolio of customers in aviation and defense, healthcare, pharmaceutical manufacturing, technology, food processing, refrigeration and advanced manufacturing, supported by industry-leading engineering, preconstruction and fabrication capabilities. Murphy's experienced management team, led by President and Chief Executive Officer Patrick Murphy, will remain in place following the Transaction.

In addition to its large-scale construction capabilities, Murphy maintains a substantial service and maintenance business providing recurring HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, controls and other mechanical services to mission-critical facilities as well as other market sectors. MasTec believes this business is positioned for significant growth as Murphy expands its owner-direct relationships and supports the increasing number of data centers and other large-load facilities transitioning from construction into ongoing operation. This recurring service revenue complements Murphy’s project-based operations, strengthens customer relationships and enhances the resilience and visibility of its financial performance. For the two years ended March 31, 2026, Murphy delivered strong double-digit growth in both revenue and EBITDA, driven by increasing demand for mission-critical infrastructure, strong customer relationships and consistent execution for its customers. Murphy is projected to generate full calendar year 2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $775 million and approximately $140 million, respectively. Murphy will serve as a new operating group of MasTec, and Murphy’s financial results are expected to be reflected in the Clean Energy and Infrastructure Segment.

Jose Mas, MasTec’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, "We are excited to welcome Murphy and its talented team members to the MasTec family. Murphy has built one of the premier integrated mechanical contracting businesses in the United States through exceptional customer service, operational excellence and an unwavering commitment to safety. Just as importantly, Murphy has built a culture that closely aligns with MasTec's values, including a commitment to entrepreneurship, accountability, safety, long-term relationships and taking care of its people.

“Murphy expands MasTec’s capabilities in some of the fastest growing and most diverse infrastructure markets in North America. Its highly skilled union craft workforce, supported by established apprenticeship, training and field-leadership programs, provides the labor capacity and execution expertise required to deliver large, complex projects safely and efficiently. Together, we will be able to provide customers with a broader range of self-perform infrastructure services across both the construction and operational phases of mission-critical facilities.

“We believe Murphy's differentiated market position, strong recurring service and maintenance revenue, attractive margin profile and substantial growth opportunities make it an exceptional strategic fit for MasTec and a highly compelling investment for our shareholders."

Patrick Murphy, President and CEO of Murphy, commented, “For over 100 years, our family has had the privilege of leading a company built by outstanding employees and trusted by exceptional customers. As we considered the future of Murphy, it was important to find a partner that shared our commitment to safety, integrity, operational excellence and enduring relationships.

“We found that partner in the MasTec family. Their reputation for execution, entrepreneurial culture and commitment to investing in people made this a natural fit. By joining MasTec, we will be able to provide additional opportunities for our employees, expand the capabilities we bring to our customers and continue building on the legacy that has defined Murphy for more than a century.

“Most importantly, our customers, employees and partners can expect continuity from the team and culture that have made Murphy successful, while benefiting from the scale and resources of one of North America's leading infrastructure companies.”

Transaction Rationale

Expands MasTec's Participation Across Mission-Critical Infrastructure: Murphy adds leading mechanical, plumbing, HVAC and process infrastructure capabilities serving highly attractive and diverse end markets. Together, MasTec and Murphy will provide a broader range of self-perform infrastructure solutions “inside the fence”.

Adds A Scarce, Scaled Mechanical Infrastructure Platform: Murphy is among the largest mechanical contractors in the United States, with over 100 years of operating history, approximately 1,600 employees, including approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals, national execution capabilities and one of the most experienced leadership teams in the industry. Opportunities to acquire assets of this scale and quality are infrequent.

Enhances Technical Capabilities and Execution Certainty: Murphy brings differentiated engineering, preconstruction, virtual design, prefabrication capabilities and building information modeling that support project execution, labor productivity, schedule certainty and quality performance. These capabilities create meaningful value for customers and represent significant barriers to entry within the industry.

Highly Complementary Culture and Leadership Team: Murphy's family ownership, people-first culture, commitment to safety and operational excellence closely align with MasTec's values and operating philosophy. The Transaction preserves an experienced leadership team while providing additional resources to support continued growth and long-term customer success.

Deepens Relationships with Leading Infrastructure Customers: Murphy serves a diversified base of blue-chip customers and project partners across critical infrastructure markets, supported by longstanding relationships and a proven track record delivering large, complex projects safely and successfully. The combination creates opportunities to expand services with existing customers and pursue larger opportunities together.

Immediate Financial Contributions with Significant Long-Term Growth Opportunities: Murphy has demonstrated a consistent track record of growth, profitability and cash flow generation supported by strong backlog visibility, recurring service and maintenance revenue and favorable long-term trends across its end markets. MasTec expects meaningful opportunities to expand Murphy’s service business by supporting the growing installed base of operational data centers and other diverse facilities, including facilities where Murphy’s construction relationships and knowledge provide a natural foundation for ongoing maintenance and support. MasTec expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, earnings per share and cash flow from operations.

Transaction Overview

The purchase price is approximately $1.25 billion payable in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments. Additionally, there is a potential earnout payment based on the cumulative three-year financial performance of Murphy post-closing. MasTec has arranged to finance the Transaction with a bank term loan entered into contemporaneously with the Transaction agreement. MasTec’s September 30, 2026 pro forma net leverage is estimated to be 2.7x with further deleveraging expected to reduce net leverage to less than 2.0x during calendar year 2027. Substantially all conditions to closing have been satisfied and MasTec expects to close the transaction expeditiously.

McDermott Will & Schulte LLP and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP are serving as MasTec's Transaction and financing legal advisors, respectively. Sable Capital, LLC is serving as financial advisor to Murphy, and Holland & Knight LLP as its legal advisor.

About MasTec

MasTec, Inc. is a leading North American infrastructure engineering and construction company focused primarily on engineering, building, installation, maintenance and upgrade of communications, energy and utility and other infrastructure. MasTec primarily operates under four business segments including Communications, serving both wireless and wireline/fiber infrastructure; Power Delivery, serving primarily utility customers in transmission, distribution and large load electrical infrastructure markets; Pipeline Infrastructure serving energy and other customers with installation and maintenance services primarily for natural gas pipeline and distribution infrastructure; and Clean Energy and Infrastructure, providing renewable energy engineering and construction services, as well as for heavy civil and other industrial infrastructure markets. Learn more at www.mastec.com.

Murphy is a premier national contractor designing, constructing, and maintaining mechanical systems for the commercial, industrial, and institutional markets with unique capabilities to manage complex and demanding projects. We continually innovate and improve our business processes to maximize value for our customers and to better our company’s performance. WeRide Inc. Announces Unaudited Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- WeRide Inc. (“WeRide” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: WRD; HKEX: 0800), a global leader in autonomous driving technology, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Operational and Financial Highlights

  • Revenue grew 88.0% and gross margin expanded to 43.0%, driven primarily by the overseas business. Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB321.5 million (US$48.0 million), representing an increase of 88.0% year over year and 38.8% quarter over quarter. Gross margin reached 43.0%, up 10.1 percentage points year over year. Revenue from higher-margin overseas operations was RMB146.9 million (US$21.9 million), up 171.5% year over year, and accounted for 45.7% of total revenue.
  • AI Infrastructure revenue nearly doubled, capturing fast-growing data demand from Physical AI. Leveraging the closed‑loop data capabilities built over years of autonomous‑driving operations, Jingshuo Technology, WeRide’s Physical AI Infrastructure (“AI Infrastructure”) subsidiary, serves customers across embodied AI, robotics, autonomous driving and foundation models, with end‑to‑end solutions spanning pre‑training data, post‑training environments and trusted verification. Driven by surging demand for high-quality physical-world data, revenue from this business nearly doubled year over year.
  • Quarterly Robotaxi revenue surpassed RMB100 million; Guangzhou operations achieved positive unit economics. In the third quarter of 2026, Robotaxi revenue exceeded RMB100 million for the first time, up 204.0% year over year, with overseas markets contributing more than 90% of total Robotaxi revenue. The Company’s Robotaxi operations in Guangzhou achieved positive unit economics, marking an important milestone in validating the economics of Robotaxi operations at scale.
  • Global L4 fleet of approximately 4,100 vehicles; Robotaxi fleet up 26% quarter over quarter. As of October 31, 2026, the Company’s global L4 fleet comprised approximately 4,100 vehicles, including more than 2,300 Robotaxis. The Robotaxi fleet increased by 26% quarter over quarter.
  • WeRide secured Spain’s first national operating permit for L4 autonomous passenger vehicles, accelerating commercialization in Europe. The Company received Spain’s first L4 autonomous passenger vehicle operating permit from the Spanish Directorate-General for Traffic (“DGT”), laying the groundwork for commercial services in Spain. The Company also advanced its operations in Switzerland, Belgium and France, and began road testing in Slovakia, while continuing to expand its collaboration with local public transportation operators.
  • Asset-light expansion accelerating in the Middle East, with a fleet of approximately 600 vehicles. The Company continues to expand its operating fleet and service areas in the Middle East, targeting full coverage of the core urban areas of Abu Dhabi and Dubai by year-end. The Company’s Middle East fleet reached approximately 600 vehicles, up approximately 50% from about 400 vehicles as of July 31, 2026. As of the date of this release, WeRide is Uber’s largest autonomous vehicle partner outside the United States, measured by the number of fully driverless Robotaxis operating on its platform.
  • L2++/L3 mass production accelerating, with cumulative WRD 3.0 deliveries exceeding 100,000 units. Now, the AION i60, GAC Trumpchi Yue 7 and AION Ray7, all equipped with the Company’s WRD 3.0 one-stage end-to-end L2++/L3 solution, were launched, extending the solution’s adoption across more production models and driving scenarios. By the end of the quarter, cumulative deliveries of WRD 3.0 exceeded 100,000 units. The Company continued to expand its partnership network, establishing collaborations with several leading OEM groups.

L4 Business Update

Robotaxi Business Update

In the third quarter of 2026, Robotaxi revenue exceeded RMB100 million for the first time, representing an increase of 204.0% year over year, with overseas markets contributing more than 90% of total Robotaxi revenue.

International Operations

  • Overseas Robotaxi revenue grew rapidly, supported by the Company’s high-margin, asset-light business model. In overseas markets, the Company provides autonomous driving technology and remote assistance, while local partners provide fleet investment and handle other operations. This division of roles enables the Company to continue scaling deployments across Europe and the Middle East with greater capital efficiency.
  • The Middle East fleet expanded, with broader coverage of core urban areas. The Company continued to expand its Middle East fleet to approximately 600 Robotaxis and extend its operating areas in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, now covering the major districts of both cities’ core urban areas. This lays the foundation for broader service coverage and future operational growth.
  • WeRide obtained Spain’s first national L4 autonomous driving permit and advanced its Madrid deployment. In September 2026, the Company, together with Uber and AVOMO, received Spain's first L4 autonomous passenger vehicle operating permit from the DGT, allowing vehicles to be deployed on public roads. The permit authorizes testing of WeRide’s GXR autonomous vehicles in Spain and marks the beginning of mapping in the Madrid region ahead of the Company’s first joint launch in Europe.
  • L4 deployments and services in Switzerland and Slovakia continued to advance. Along with its partners, Schweizerische Bundesbahnen (“SBB”) and Swiss Transit Lab (“STL”), the Company launched public Robotaxi services in Canton of Zurich. In Slovakia, the first batch of Robotaxis began road testing, building operating experience to support future deployments.
  • Robotaxi services in Asia continued to expand. In Singapore, the Company continued to expand its Robotaxi service together with Grab and had provided more than 20,000 L4 autonomous driving rides as of the end of the third quarter of 2026.

China Operations

  • Guangzhou operations achieved positive unit economics, with further improvements in operational efficiency. In the third quarter of 2026, domestic Robotaxi operations achieved an average of 21 daily orders per vehicle, with a peak of 33 orders per vehicle in one day. Cumulative registered users continued to grow rapidly, up 143.5% from the end of the previous quarter.
  • Service areas in key cities continued to expand. In Guangzhou, the Company’s Robotaxi service covers Tianhe, Haizhu and the core districts of Huangpu. These developments provide a solid foundation for further scaling the Company’s Robotaxi business.

Other L4 Business Updates

  • Robobus achieved one of Europe’s first fully driverless services. At Zurich Airport, the Company’s Robobus now operates without an onboard safety operator, making it one of the first fully driverless Robobus services in Europe. The Company is also advancing autonomous driving collaborations with public transportation operators such as Keolis in France and expanding its Robobus operations in Belgium. In Slovakia, the Robobus fleet has arrived and commenced testing.
  • Robosweeper expanded its presence in Singapore. The Company has partnered with leading environmental services providers, Chye Thiam Maintenance and RE Sustainability, to deliver sanitation services across key locations including Marina Coastal Drive, the Esplanade and Sentosa Island, with further deployments expected in the near term.

L2++/L3 Business Update

  • Cumulative deliveries exceeded 100,000 units, with a growing mass-production pipeline. As of the end of the quarter, cumulative deliveries of the Company’s WRD 3.0 L2++/L3 solution exceeded 100,000 units. During the quarter, the Company secured 10 new L2++/L3 mass-production design wins, further expanding its pipeline of future production programs.
  • Customer base and design-win portfolio continued to expand. The Company secured multiple new design wins from several leading OEMs, further validating the competitiveness of its technology and expanding its customer reach.
  • The Company’s L2++/L3 solution continued to demonstrate its capabilities in driving competitions. Customer vehicles equipped with the Company’s L2++/L3 solution have won eight championships in the China Intelligent Driving Competition, further demonstrating the solution’s overall technical capabilities.

AI Infrastructure Business Update

High-quality real-world data and verifiable training environments are key enablers for the development of Physical AI foundation models.

  • End-to-end capabilities covering the full path from pre-training to continuous learning. Building on the closed-loop data capabilities developed through the Company’s autonomous driving operations, Jingshuo provides pre-training data, post-training environments and trusted verification across the full path from pre-training to continuous learning. Its capabilities span data collection, quality control and annotation, synthetic data generation, environment construction, independent evaluation and post-training integration. It offers high-quality datasets, licensing of data-processing software and post-training environments, and customized data services to customers in autonomous driving, foundation models, embodied AI and robotics.
  • A three-layer product suite and two engines, closing the “collection–assetization–training” loop.  Jingshuo’s product stack comprises three layers. EGOK is a proprietary wearable multimodal collection terminal with hardware-level synchronization. SkillForge turns first-person operation data into trainable, verifiable and licensable skill assets with task definitions and success criteria. Crucible is an environment hub that connects tasks into executable, independently judged environments and supports post-training integration. Two engines connect the layers: the Data Engine turns experience into versioned data and skills, and the World Engine, powered by the GENESIS-Robotics world model, turns real-world demonstrations into verifiable training environments.
  • High-quality multimodal data assets support applications across diverse real-world scenarios. Through automated 3D reconstruction, multimodal alignment and fine-grained annotation, Jingshuo has built a large-scale dataset library serving foundation model, embodied AI and robotics customers in China and overseas.

Management Commentary

Tony Han, WeRide’s Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer, stated, “This quarter showed that our global strategy is working. Overseas markets now generate nearly half of our total revenue and more than 90% of our Robotaxi revenue. Operating driverless fleets in foreign markets is challenging, which is exactly why it is becoming our long-term moat. With new deployments in Europe and a Middle East fleet of approximately 600 vehicles, WeRide is now Uber’s largest autonomous vehicle partner outside the United States by driverless fleet size. In China, our Guangzhou Robotaxi operations achieved positive unit economics, demonstrating that Robotaxi can be a sustainable business. Robotaxi is our core business and the fastest path to commercializing Physical AI. The technology and closed-loop data we have built on real roads now power three mutually reinforcing businesses: Robotaxi, L2++/L3 solutions, and AI Infrastructure, which extends these capabilities to foundation models, embodied AI and robotics. As an infrastructure builder for Physical AI, we are just getting started.”

Jennifer Li, WeRide’s Chief Financial Officer and Head of International, added, “This quarter, revenue grew by 88% to RMB321.5 million, gross margin reached 43%, and overseas revenue made up nearly half of the total. Our asset-light model enables us to expand quickly and efficiently. Based on our operating plan, we have more than four years of cash runway, sufficient to fully fund our path to self-sustaining cash flow. More importantly, we are building a long-term moat. Operating across 13 countries and holding permits in 9 requires years of regulatory trust and operational experience — this is hard to replicate. We will translate this lead into sustainable, profitable growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenue

Total revenue grew 88.0% year over year to RMB321.5 million (US$48.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB171.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the expansion of the Company’s Robotaxi-centered L4 business, rapid growth in the L2++/L3 business and continued growth in the AI Infrastructure business.

Cost of Revenue

Cost of revenue was RMB183.4 million (US$27.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB114.7 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in cost of revenue was in line with revenue growth in the Robotaxi-centered L4 business and the AI Infrastructure business.

Gross Profit and Gross Margin

Gross profit was RMB138.1 million (US$20.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB56.3 million in the same period of 2025. Gross margin was 43.0% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 32.9% in the same period of 2025. Gross margin expansion was mainly driven by revenue growth in the high-margin overseas business and the L2++/L3 business.

Operating Expenses

Operating expenses were RMB505.7 million (US$75.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB435.8 million in the same period of 2025.

  • R&D expenses were RMB465.3 million (US$69.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB316.4 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in R&D expenses was primarily due to the increase in personnel and outsourcing labor costs, outsourced R&D expenses and cloud service fees. In addition, from July 1, 2026, the estimated useful lives of IDC-related equipment were uniformly extended to six years, resulting in lower depreciation and amortization expenses.
     
  • Administrative expenses were RMB13.9 million (US$2.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB100.4 million in the same period of 2025. The significant decrease in administrative expenses was primarily due to a reversal of share-based compensation expenses resulting from employee departures, and a decrease in professional service fees, as the same period of 2025 included fees related to the global offering.
     
  • Selling expenses were RMB26.5 million (US$4.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB19.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in selling expenses was primarily due to the increase in sales personnel costs.

Loss for the Period

  • Loss for the period was RMB310.0 million (US$46.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB307.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-IFRS adjusted loss1 for the period was RMB336.5 million (US$50.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB275.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (“EBITDA”)2

EBITDA was negative RMB246.4 million (US$36.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, an improvement of 2.9% from negative RMB253.7 million in the same period of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Loss per Ordinary Share and per ADS3  

  • Basic and diluted loss per ordinary share was RMB0.32 (US$0.05) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.34 in the same period of 2025.
     
  • Basic and diluted loss per ADS was RMB0.96 (US$0.15) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB1.02 in the same period of 2025.

KEARNEY, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Buckle, Inc. (NYSE: BKE) announced today that net income for the fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis).

Net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.6 percent to $329.2 million from net sales of $320.8 million for the prior year 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 0.6 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 13-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales decreased 1.4 percent to $52.2 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $53.0 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Net sales for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 increased 4.3 percent to $937.8 million from net sales of $898.7 million for the prior year 39-week fiscal period ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.5 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 39-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales increased 1.1 percent to $144.5 million for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $142.9 million for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Net income for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $48.7 million, or $0.97 per share ($0.96 per share on a diluted basis) for the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Net income for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 was $139.3 million, or $2.75 per share ($2.73 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $128.9 million, or $2.57 per share ($2.55 per share on a diluted basis) for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

ERAS-0015 at 32 mg QD achieved 44% confirmed ORR in 2L+ KRAS G12X PDAC, despite heavy pretreatment (84% in the 3L+ setting) and a high proportion of G12R mutations (44% of patients)

ERAS-0015 at 32 mg QD achieved 69% confirmed ORR in 2L+ KRAS G12D or G12V PDAC

ERAS-0015 at 32 mg QD achieved 60% confirmed ORR in post-ICI/platinum (2L/3L) KRAS G12X NSCLC

ERAS-0015 at 32 mg QD continued to be generally well tolerated, with mostly low-grade TRAEs and low rates of dose interruptions, reductions, and discontinuations

Early combination data with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, pembrolizumab, and panitumumab support ERAS-0015’s combination backbone potential

ERAS-4001 showed preliminary Phase 1 antitumor activity, favorable tolerability, and encouraging PK; dose escalation of the ERAS-0015 + ERAS-4001 combination expected to initiate in 2027

Conference call and live webcast today at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Erasca, Inc. (Nasdaq: ERAS), a clinical-stage precision oncology company singularly focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing therapies for patients with RAS/MAPK pathway-driven cancers, today announced positive updated U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy and initial combination data reinforcing the best-in-class potential of pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. The Company confirms its plans to initiate a potentially registration-enabling trial in 2L+ lung cancer in the first half of 2027 and a Phase 3 trial in 1L lung cancer in the second half of 2027 to first half of 2028 timeframe; and is accelerating the planned initiation of a Phase 3 trial in 1L pancreatic cancer to the first half of 2027. The Company also announced encouraging initial U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy data for potential first-in-class pan-KRAS inhibitor ERAS-4001, supporting its combination potential with ERAS-0015.

"These compelling results highlight the strength and breadth of ERAS-0015’s clinical activity across several tumor types," said Jonathan E. Lim, M.D., Erasca’s chairman, CEO, and co-founder. “We are particularly encouraged by confirmed responses in common KRAS mutation subtypes, including G12D and G12V, which together occur in nearly 70% of patients with pancreatic cancer. Importantly, we believe the robust clinical activity observed in this heavily pretreated population, which included a high proportion of patients whose tumors harbored less sensitive mutations, compares favorably with reported activity for other pan-RAS and mutant-selective inhibitors, subject to the limitations of cross-study comparisons. Additionally, we believe these efficacy results, coupled with generally well-tolerated safety data and low rates of dose interruptions, reductions, and discontinuations at 32 mg once daily, support advancing ERAS-0015 toward multiple potentially registration-enabling trials."

Dr. Lim continued, “Early combination data demonstrating favorable tolerability results with chemotherapy, an immune checkpoint inhibitor, and an anti-EGFR antibody, together with preliminary clinical activity for ERAS-4001, strengthen our rationale for expanding ERAS-0015’s combination potential. We expect 2027 to be an important year for our RAS-targeting franchise as we plan to initiate potentially registration-enabling clinical trials in pancreatic and lung cancers and advance combination dose-escalation trials, including the planned ERAS-0015 plus ERAS-4001 combination.”

Key U.S. Phase 1 interim results for ERAS-0015 (AURORAS-1):

As of the data cutoff date, ERAS-0015 monotherapy at the pharmacologically active doses (PAD) of 16-32 mg once daily (QD) (N=122) was generally well-tolerated with favorable safety data, and demonstrated encouraging activity in key KRAS G12X tumors. Monotherapy responses shown are confirmed. All patients with responses at 32 mg QD in all tumor types remained on treatment.1,2

ERAS-0015 Monotherapy Showed Strong Anti-Tumor Activity Across Advanced KRAS-Mutant Cancers

  • KRAS G12X pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) at 32 mg QD in the second-line or greater (2L+) setting1,2
    • 44% confirmed objective response rate (ORR) across all patients (N=25) with KRAS G12X mutations; 84% were treated in the third-line or later (3L+) setting and 44% had G12R mutations
    • 69% confirmed ORR in patients (N=13) with KRAS G12D or G12V PDAC, which represent nearly 70% of patients with PDAC. Of these patients, 77% were treated in 3L+

      • 63% confirmed ORR (N=8) in patients with KRAS G12D
      • 80% confirmed ORR (N=5) in patients with KRAS G12V
    • All (11 of 11) patients with confirmed responses and 6 of 11 patients with stable disease remained on treatment
  • KRAS G12X non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)1,2
    • 60% confirmed ORR (N=5) at 32 mg QD and 58% confirmed ORR (N=12) across the PAD range of 16-32 mg QD in the 2L or 3L setting following an immune checkpoint inhibitor and platinum-based chemotherapy (post-ICI/platinum)
    • Activity was observed across multiple KRAS mutation subtypes at 32 mg QD in the 2L+ setting:

      • 60% confirmed ORR (N=5) in patients with KRAS G12D mutations
      • 50% confirmed ORR (N=4) in patients with KRAS G12V mutations
    • At 32 mg QD in the 2L+ setting, all (5 of 5) patients with confirmed responses and all (5 of 5) patients with stable disease remained on treatment
  • KRAS G12X biliary tract cancer (BTC) at 32 mg QD in the 1L+ setting1
    • 75% confirmed ORR (N=4)
    • All (3 of 3) patients with confirmed responses remained on treatment

ERAS-0015 Monotherapy Continued to Be Generally Well-Tolerated with Favorable Safety Data in Expanded Patient Population1,5

  • Frequency and severity of treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) remained consistent with the Company’s April and July 2026 interim data disclosures
  • Mostly low-grade TRAEs with no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and low rate of dose interruptions, reductions, and discontinuations due to TRAEs
    • At 32 mg QD (N=54), TRAEs led to dose interruptions in 13.0% of patients and dose reductions in 16.7% of patients, and there were no dose discontinuations (0% of patients)
  • 100% median relative dose intensity (RDI) at 32 mg QD

Early ERAS-0015 Combination Data Support Further Development and Potential for Differentiation with Standard-of-Care Therapies3

  • ERAS-0015 plus gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (Days 1 and 15):
    • Generally well tolerated with favorable safety data and no unexpected safety signals
    • The DLT window was cleared through the 16 mg QD ERAS-0015 cohort with no DLTs
    • Currently dosing the 24 mg QD ERAS-0015 dose escalation cohort
    • Efficacy data not yet available
    • Clinical data support further development in 1L PDAC
  • ERAS-0015 plus pembrolizumab:
    • Generally well tolerated with favorable safety data and no unexpected safety signals
    • The DLT window was cleared through the 32 mg QD ERAS-0015 cohort with no DLTs
    • Multiple responses observed in multiple solid tumor types in dose escalation
    • Clinical data support further development in 1L NSCLC, including combination with carboplatin/pemetrexed/pembrolizumab (initiated in Q4)
  • ERAS-0015 plus panitumumab:
    • 16 mg QD ERAS-0015 was generally well tolerated with favorable safety data and no unexpected safety signals
    • Multiple responses were observed in dose escalation in patients with KRAS G12X colorectal cancer (CRC), including 2 ongoing confirmed partial responses (PR) in 2 patients treated at 24 mg QD who then dose reduced to 16 mg QD, and 1 unconfirmed PR (uPR) in 4 patients treated at 16 mg QD
    • Combination dose exploration ongoing; plan to make dose selection in 2027

Encouraging Preliminary ERAS-4001 Phase 1 Data Support Planned Combination with ERAS-00154

  • Favorable safety and tolerability data with predominantly low-grade adverse events and no TRAEs leading to treatment discontinuation
  • Pharmacokinetic (PK) results were encouraging and support continued dose escalation
  • Preliminary monotherapy antitumor activity supports ERAS-4001’s potential as a combination partner for ERAS-0015
  • Nonclinical data demonstrated that the combination of ERAS-0015 and ERAS-4001 targets both active- and inactive-state KRAS and exhibits synergistic activity in KRAS G12X-driven models, providing a rationale for further evaluation of this combination

Key Anticipated Milestones

ERAS-0015: AURORAS-1 and Phase 3 Trials

  • Potentially registration-enabling trial in patients with 2L+ RAS-mutant NSCLC expected to initiate in the first half of 2027
  • Phase 3 trial in patients with 1L PDAC accelerated to initiate in the first half of 2027
  • Phase 3 trial in patients with 1L RAS-mutant NSCLC expected to initiate in the second half of 2027 to the first half of 2028
  • Combination dose escalation and expansion data expected in 2027

ERAS-4001: BOREALIS-1 Trial

  • Initiation of combination dose escalation trial with ERAS-0015 planned for 2027

¹ Data cutoff date (DCO) September 1, 2026
² Includes responses confirmed after the data cutoff date
3 DCO October 14, 2026

5 As disclosed by the Company in April 2026, one Grade 3 TRAE of pneumonitis progressed to Grade 5 after withdrawal of supportive care per patient decision. The patient was a 66 year-old male with heavily pretreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who received 24 mg of ERAS-0015. The patient had pulmonary metastases, a history of right lung cryoablation and no history of lung radiation. The patient presented to the ER approximately a month after starting ERAS-0015 with Grade 3 pneumonitis that was treated aggressively with immediate discontinuation of ERAS-0015, high dose steroids and infliximab. The patient requested withdrawal of supportive care and ultimately died of the event. No additional Grade 5 TRAEs have occurred

Erasca will hold a virtual investor event today, Friday, November 20, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. To register for the event please click here. The live webcast and replay may be accessed by referring to Erasca’s website at Erasca.com/events.

About ERAS-0015
ERAS-0015 is an investigational, oral, highly potent pan-RAS molecular glue designed to inhibit RAS signaling with a potential best-in-class profile and has received Fast Track Designation (FTD) from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The ongoing AURORAS-1 Phase 1 trial is evaluating ERAS-0015 as a monotherapy and in combination with other therapies in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. Clinical data have demonstrated robust monotherapy activity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and encouraging initial activity in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer (CRC) in combination with an anti-EGFR antibody. ERAS-0015 has been generally well-tolerated with favorable safety data and with well-behaved pharmacokinetics (PK). Emerging tolerability data with chemotherapy, pembrolizumab, and panitumumab support combination development at ERAS-0015 doses within the pharmacologically active dose (PAD) range. ERAS-0015 is also designed to inhibit RAS wildtype variants, which may contribute to resistance to mutant-selective approaches. Together, these findings support its potential as both a monotherapy and backbone for combination regimens. 

About ERAS-4001
ERAS-4001 is an investigational, oral, highly potent, and selective pan-KRAS inhibitor with a potential first-in-class and best-in-class profile. Erasca is evaluating ERAS-4001 in the BOREALIS-1 Phase 1 trial in patients with KRAS-mutant solid tumors. Preliminary clinical data have demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability across doses evaluated. Promising preliminary pharmacokinetic (PK) data have been observed. In nonclinical studies, ERAS-4001 showed potent activity against both guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-bound (active state) and GDP-bound (inactive state) KRAS and induced tumor regression in multiple KRAS-mutant models. ERAS-4001 also inhibited wildtype KRAS, which may contribute to resistance to mutant-selective approaches, while sparing wildtype HRAS and NRAS. Preliminary monotherapy antitumor activity supports ERAS-4001’s potential as a combination partner for ERAS-0015.

About Erasca
At Erasca, our name is our mission: To erase cancer. We are a clinical-stage precision oncology company singularly focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing therapies for patients with RAS/MAPK pathway-driven cancers. Our company was co-founded by leading pioneers in precision oncology and RAS targeting to create novel therapies and combination regimens designed to comprehensively shut down the RAS/MAPK pathway for the treatment of patients with cancer. We believe our team’s capabilities and experience, further guided by our scientific advisory board which includes the world’s leading experts in the RAS/MAPK pathway, uniquely position us to achieve our bold mission of erasing cancer.

SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PayPal Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: PYPL) today announced that Brian J. Lee will join the company's Board of Directors as of November 30, 2026.

Lee brings more than three decades of experience in financial services, including serving as Chief Risk Officer at Goldman Sachs, where he developed deep expertise in enterprise risk management, financial oversight, regulatory capital, and corporate governance.

"Brian's extensive experience overseeing risk at one of the world's leading financial institutions makes him an outstanding addition to our Board," said David Dorman, Chair of PayPal's Board of Directors. "His financial acumen, understanding of complex global financial institutions and commitment to strong governance will provide important perspective as we continue to advance PayPal's long-term strategy and deliver value for our shareholders."

"PayPal is at an important inflection point as we sharpen our focus on financial services, strengthen our businesses, and reimagine how we serve consumers and merchants," said Enrique Lores, President and CEO of PayPal. "Brian's perspective on the evolving financial services landscape will be valuable as we execute our three-year strategy and deliver on the commitments we've made to our customers and shareholders."

"I'm honored to join PayPal's Board of Directors as the company enters its next chapter," said Lee. "PayPal serves as a financial partner that customers trust, connecting hundreds of millions of consumers and merchants through its payments platform. I look forward to working with Enrique, David, and my fellow directors to support the company's strategy, strengthen its competitive position and drive long-term value creation."

Lee joined Goldman Sachs in 1994 and has held numerous senior leadership positions at the firm. Most recently, he served as Chairman of its Risk Council from 2025 to October 2026, following his role as Chief Risk Officer from 2019 to January 2025. Previously, he served as Controller and Chief Accounting Officer from 2017 to 2019, overseeing financial reporting, product control, and regulatory capital. He was named Managing Director in 2002 and Partner in 2008. Prior to Goldman Sachs, Lee worked at Price Waterhouse. He also serves on the Board of Directors of KKR & Co. Inc.

Frontier Minerals consortium to enter exclusive negotiations with Government of Kenya for prospecting licence for Mrima Hill, one of the world’s largest and highest grade rare earth projects,¹ and concurrently pursue potential non-dilutive funding including U.S. Government grant support.

KELLOGG, Idaho, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bunker Hill Silver Corp. ("Bunker Hill" or the "Company") (TSX: BNKR | OTCQB: BHLL) is pleased to announce that Frontier Minerals LLC ("Frontier"), a U.S.-led consortium which includes Bunker Hill alongside ReElement Technologies Corporation ("ReElement") and American Resources Corporation (“American Resources”) (NASDAQ: AREC), has received notification from the Government of Kenya's Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs (the "Ministry") that it is the successful bidder in the international tender for the exclusive right to negotiate a prospecting licence for the Mrima Hill Rare Earth and Niobium Project in Kwale County, Kenya ("Mrima Hill" or the "Project"). The Cabinet Secretary for Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs announced the outcome of the tender on November 19, 2026.

Frontier is partnered with Bunker Hill, ReElement and American Resources, bringing together complementary expertise in mineral resource development, critical minerals supply chains and advanced refining technologies. Bunker Hill and the other consortium partners are expected to hold equity interests in Frontier, with the specific terms of the joint venture to be set forth in definitive agreements. Frontier is also pursuing U.S. government funding through the U.S. Department of State’s U.S.-Africa Strategic Investment Program for Project support. Subject to confirmation in definitive agreements, Bunker Hill does not anticipate a material cash outlay from the Company in the near-term or throughout the Mrima Hill feasibility study completion.

Mrima Hill is the first mining project in Kenya to be offered through an open and competitive international tender. Frontier's proposal combines Bunker Hill's mine-building and operating capability, as the consortium's mining and processing partner, with the innovative American refining capabilities and rare earth and critical minerals supply chain relationships contributed by ReElement and American Resources, a model designed to deliver separated rare earth and niobium products refined in Kenya for Western supply chains.

Under the proposed development plan submitted through the tender process, and if the consortium is ultimately awarded a prospecting licence for the Project, Bunker Hill will lead exploration and resource definition, metallurgical test work, process development and the feasibility study, which it will manage. Bunker Hill is also positioned to be contracted by the consortium to build and operate the mine and processing plant for Frontier in accordance with the results of the feasibility study. To maintain the Bunker Hill Mine team’s focus on the commissioning of the Bunker Hill operations in Idaho, the Project exploration, feasibility study, development and operations will be overseen and managed by a dedicated team assembled specifically for Mrima Hill in Kenya.

Bunker Hill will host a conference call and webcast on Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 am Eastern Time. Details are provided below.

Highlights

  • Capital light participation: Bunker Hill expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier, subject to definitive agreements. The Frontier consortium is pursuing potential U.S. government financing for the Project and Bunker Hill does not expect to be required to make material cash contributions through completion of a feasibility study. Subject to confirmation through definitive agreements among the consortium partners, Bunker Hill expects to maintain the right but not the obligation to fund Project development.
  • World-scale, two-metal deposit: Historical 2013 NI 43-101 estimates of 48.7 Mt Indicated at 4.40% Total Rare Earth Oxides (TREO) and 110.7 Mt Inferred at 3.61% TREO (1.0% TREO cut-off), and 47.8 Mt Indicated at 0.66% Nb2O5 and 94.4 Mt Inferred at 0.73% Nb2O5 (0.2% Nb2O5 cut-off)², all from surface (historical estimates; not current mineral resources; see “Historical Mineral Resource Estimates” below).
  • Approximately 7% TREO from surface: Historical estimates include higher-grade domains of 11.2 Mt Indicated at 6.93% TREO and 15.6 Mt Inferred at 7.12% TREO at a 5.8% TREO cut-off².
  • Thick high-grade intercepts and open for expansion: Historical drilling returned 105 m at 6.97% TREO from surface, ending in mineralization and including 35 m at 8.50% TREO². Mineralization is open at depth, with rare earth and niobium mineralization reported more than 100 m below surface, and open to the south at the south-eastern margin of the deposit.
  • Rich in high-value magnet metals: Approximately 21% of the historical Indicated TREO is made up of neodymium, dysprosium, europium, terbium and yttrium oxides, with heavy rare earth enrichment relative to typical carbonatite deposits.
  • Coastal location near East Africa’s largest port: Mrima Hill is approximately 60 km by road from the Port of Mombasa and 10 km from the Indian Ocean coast. The project sits near the Mombasa–Lunga Lunga highway, which connects directly to the port.
  • Strategic U.S. critical minerals: Rare earths and niobium are both on the U.S. 2025 List of Critical Minerals. USGS ranks niobium, dysprosium, terbium, yttrium and gadolinium among the highest-risk minerals on that list. Frontier has proposed, subject to confirmation through the feasibility study, to produce separated products refined in Kenya.
  • Fast-track work program: If awarded the licence, Frontier’s 36-month work program will start with twin and confirmation drilling of the historical holes, with the aim of delivering a current NI 43-101 mineral resource within the first year. Expansion drilling, metallurgical test work and the environmental and social impact assessment follow. Frontier is targeting a feasibility study and a development decision within three years of the licence being issued.
  • Refining technology chosen on the evidence: The feasibility study, managed by Bunker Hill, will include a rigorous trade-off study of refining technologies. Subject to its results, ReElement’s chromatography-based separation technology may be used to refine the Project’s rare earths and niobium in Kenya.
  • Dedicated Mrima Hill Team:  Frontier has assembled a project team with experience on carbonatite rare earth and niobium deposits across Africa, Europe and North America. The Bunker Hill Mine team in Idaho will remain fully focused on ramping up to commercial production at the Bunker Hill Mine.
  • Potential U.S. Government funding: Mrima Hill represents a strategic asset to western governments, Frontier holds established and deep relationships within the U.S. government and has been invited to submit an application for grant funding to the U.S. Department of State.

Management Commentary

Richard Williams, Executive Chairman of Bunker Hill, commented: “Mrima Hill is one of the world’s great undeveloped rare earth deposits, and we are proud to have been chosen to help unlock it. In Idaho we are bringing a mine that had been closed for four decades back into production. We along with our consortium partners are bringing that same capability, and a dedicated team, to Kenya, while the Bunker Hill Mine stays fully focused on ramping up to commercial production. This is a defining step in building Bunker Hill into a leading Western supplier of critical minerals.”

Bradley Barnett, CFO of Bunker Hill and Managing Member of Frontier, added: “Kenya ran the first open and competitive mining tender in its history and set a high bar on beneficiation, transparency and community benefit. Frontier proposed a plan to deliver a current resource within a year and a feasibility study within three, and to refine separated rare earth and niobium products in Kenya. We thank Cabinet Secretary Joho, the Ministry and the people of Kwale County for their confidence. We look forward to working with the communities of Kwale County and the Ministry through the licensing process and getting to work.”

Mark C. Jensen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Resources and ReElement Technologies, added: "We are proud to partner with Bunker Hill and Frontier Minerals on this significant opportunity. By combining world-class mining expertise with advanced American refining technologies and integrated critical mineral supply-chain capabilities, we believe we can establish a new model for resource development that enables Kenya to capture greater economic value from its mineral resources while strengthening secure supply chains for the United States and its allies. This selection is not the culmination of our efforts, but the beginning of a long-term partnership focused on responsible development, economic opportunity and shared prosperity."

U.S. Government Support, Strategic Importance and Community Engagement

Frontier is a U.S.-led consortium. Its aim is to build a secure, US-aligned supply of rare earths and niobium. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) ranks niobium, dysprosium, terbium, yttrium and gadolinium among the highest-risk minerals on the U.S. Government’s 2025 list of Critical Minerals. The United States has had no significant niobium mine production since 1959 and imports most of the rare earths it uses. China tightened export controls on rare earth elements in 2025, adding urgency to the search for independent sources. Mrima Hill, with large, high-grade rare earth and niobium mineralization from surface and direct access to a deep-water port, is positioned to become a cornerstone of that supply.

The U.S. Government has made clear its support for developing Kenya’s critical minerals sector. Senior U.S. Department of State officials have publicly backed U.S. participation in the Mrima Hill tender, described the process as transparent, and stated that Washington is ready to help Kenya build a local critical minerals processing industry and become a regional leader in the sector4. Speaking to the American Chamber of Commerce in Kenya in Nairobi on 9 September 2026, Chris Kulukundis, then Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Southern Africa and Critical Minerals, said: “The Mrima Hill tender process is moving forward in a transparent manner.” Frontier is preparing a full proposal, at the invitation of the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of African Affairs, under the Department’s publicly announced U.S.-Africa Strategic Investment Program, for Project support. No award has been made, the terms of any award are not known and there is no assurance that funding will be approved.

Bunker Hill and its consortium partners recognize the environmental and cultural significance of Mrima Hill to the Digo community and the people of Kwale County. Working with the Ministry, Frontier intends to engage openly with local communities and stakeholders as the Project advances, and to develop it responsibly and in partnership with the Government of Kenya.

Bunker Hill's Role

Under the proposed development plan submitted through the tender process Bunker Hill will be the mining and processing partner in Frontier if the consortium is awarded the prospecting licence. It will be responsible for exploration and resource definition, mine planning, metallurgical test work, process development and the feasibility study, which it will manage. ReElement and American Resources contribute innovative American refining capabilities and rare earth and critical minerals supply chain relationships. The feasibility study will include a trade-off study of refining technologies, amongst other standard trade-off studies common in a feasibility study of this type. Subject to a positive feasibility study, the grant of a Mining Licence and financing, Bunker Hill is positioned to be contracted by Frontier to build and then operate the mine and processing plant. Bunker Hill also expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier, subject to definitive agreements.

Dedicated Project Team

Frontier has assembled a team built specifically for Mrima Hill, with extensive experience on carbonatite-hosted deposits, including rare earth and niobium deposits, in the United States, Malawi, Tanzania, South Africa and Angola and Finland as well as in rare earth processing and refining technology. Resident positions, including a resource geologist and environmental and community teams, will be recruited in Kenya before the program starts.

Bunker Hill’s leadership will provide strategic oversight. Sam Ash will oversee the mining engineering work, Richard Williams will advise the Steering Committee, and Bradley Barnett will serve on the Steering Committee. The Project will be delivered by its own dedicated team, keeping the Bunker Hill Mine’s management and operating team fully focused on the ramp-up to commercial production in Idaho.

The Mrima Hill Deposit

Mrima Hill is a carbonatite complex located approximately 60 km south-west of Mombasa, capped by a thick residual (laterite) profile enriched in rare earth phosphates and pyrochlore-hosted niobium. The rare earth suite includes the high-value magnet rare earths neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium. Because the enrichment is in the residual cap, mineralization starts at surface: 83% of the tonnage in the 2011 historical estimate lay within 20 metres of surface.

The 2013 historical estimates² are modelled over a 1,500 m by 900 m footprint to 250 m depth. Drilling by Pacific Wildcat Resources Corp. (“PAW”) between 2011 and 2013 returned intercepts including 105 m at 6.97% TREO from surface, ending in mineralization and including 35 m at 8.50% TREO, and reported rare earth and niobium mineralization extending more than 100 m below surface. The deposit is open at depth and to the south. Mrima Hill has been ranked among the world’s largest rare earth projects by contained TREO¹, with grades that compare favourably with the few rare earth deposits in production or at feasibility outside China.

Seventy Years of Technical Work

Mrima Hill has been recognized as a rare earth and niobium occurrence since the 1930s, and has drawn sustained interest from major mining companies and government agencies ever since. Between 1955 and 1957, Anglo American completed approximately 1,100 m of drilling, 424 test pits, five prospect shafts and a 172 m adit. Pechiney Saint-Gobain explored the rare earths from 1967 to 1971, processing a 42-tonne bulk sample grading approximately 12% REO through its La Rochelle pilot plant to produce a 23% REO concentrate by grinding and classification alone³. The Geological Survey of Kenya, a Japanese-Kenyan joint venture and the USGS all reported on the deposit between 1959 and 19985. Between 2010 and 2012, PAW drilled 98 holes totaling approximately 7,700 m, 69 of which (5,062 m) support the 2013 historical estimates. PAW also completed the 2011 and 2013 NI 43-101 historical estimates and bench-scale leach test work, and received environmental approval for its project in 2013. Most recently, in 2022, the Government of Kenya completed a geological survey of Mrima Hill.

No pit-shell or other economic constraint was applied. The Company considers the estimates relevant as an indication of the mineralization at Mrima Hill, but their reliability cannot be confirmed until the underlying drilling, sampling, assay and QA/QC data have been obtained and verified. The Company is not aware of any more recent estimate. To verify the historical estimates or upgrade them to current mineral resources, the Company would need to obtain and verify the historical database, re-assay retained material where available, carry out confirmatory and infill drilling and density work, update the geological model, and assess reasonable prospects for eventual economic extraction, including the protected status of the Mrima Hill forest block. A qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify the historical estimates as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, and the Company is not treating them as current mineral resources or mineral reserves. These historical estimates were not prepared under S-K 1300.

Bunker Hill considers these estimates to be relevant as an indication of the scale and grade of the mineralization at Mrima Hill and reliable in that they were prepared by independent qualified persons under NI 43-101 from drilling completed to industry standards at the time. However, a qualified person acting for the consortium has not done sufficient work to classify the historical estimates as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, Bunker Hill is not treating the historical estimates as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, and the historical estimates should not be relied upon. Bunker Hill does not yet have access to the drill-hole database, assay certificates, sample material or drill core supporting the historical estimates. To verify and upgrade the historical estimates to current mineral resources, Bunker Hill would need to obtain and audit the historical data, complete twin and confirmatory drilling with current QA/QC, update the geological model and density data and have an independent qualified person prepare a new estimate, all of which form part of the consortium's planned work program. Bunker Hill is not aware of any more recent mineral resource estimate for Mrima Hill.

Next Steps and Work Program

The Ministry has stated that the award is not a licence. Before any prospecting begins, Frontier must engage openly and respectfully with host communities, landowners, county leadership and local stakeholders and obtain the consents required under Kenya’s Mining Act; apply for a prospecting licence through the Ministry’s Online Mining Cadastre; and have that application reviewed by the Mineral Rights Board, on whose recommendation the Cabinet Secretary grants the licence. Alongside that process, Frontier will also seek access to the historical drill database and core, and start recruiting its in-country team, including a resident resource geologist and environmental and community specialists.

If the Prospecting Licence is issued, Frontier will begin a 36-month work program. The first phase twins and confirms the historical PAW drill holes and is designed to deliver a current NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate within the first year. The second phase will define the broader extent of the deposit. Metallurgical test work and process development will run alongside the drilling, including a planned metallurgical testing and pilot facility in Kenya and the refining technology trade-off study, in which ReElement’s chromatography-based separation technology will be assessed. The program also includes a feasibility study and an environmental, social and health impact assessment (“ESHIA”), with a radiological baseline and radiation safety management plan, and is designed to deliver a development decision within three years of licence issue.

Conference Call and Webcast

Bunker Hill will host a conference call and webcast to discuss the Mrima Hill selection and Frontier partnership on November 23, 2026, commencing at 10:00 a.m. Toronto / 8:00 a.m. Vancouver / 7:00 a.m. Kellogg.
